Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $q\in R^{\times}$, and $H=H_{R,q}(S_n)$
([[def-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]]). Let $\Lambda$ be the set of partitions
of $n$ ordered by dominance $\unrhd$
([[def-dominance-order-on-partitions]]), and for $\lambda\in\Lambda$ let
$T(\lambda)=\mathrm{Std}(\lambda)$ be the set of standard $\lambda$-tableaux
([[def-young-tableau-standard-tableau-and-shape]]). Then the **Murphy basis
theorem** holds: the family
$$\mathcal M=\{m_{st}:\lambda\vdash n,\ s,t\in\mathrm{Std}(\lambda)\}$$
is an $R$-basis of $H$, and $(\mathcal M,\Lambda)$ is a cellular basis of $H$ in
the sense of [[def-cellular-algebra-basis-and-cell-module]]. Explicitly:
(i) $m_{st}^{*}=m_{ts}$ for all $\lambda$ and $s,t$; and (ii) for every
$\lambda$, every $t\in\mathrm{Std}(\lambda)$ and every $h\in H$ there exist
$r_v\in R$ with
$$m_{st}h\equiv\sum_{v\in\mathrm{Std}(\lambda)}r_v\,m_{sv}\pmod{H^{\rhd\lambda}},$$
where $H^{\rhd\lambda}$ is spanned by the $m_{uv}$ with $\mu\rhd\lambda$. The
theorem holds over every commutative coefficient ring with $q\in R^{\times}$
and assumes no semisimplicity; the total number of Murphy elements is
$\sum_{\lambda\vdash n}|\mathrm{Std}(\lambda)|^2=n!$
([[cor-sum-of-squares-of-standard-tableau-numbers]]), matching the rank of $H$.

In the generic type-A Hecke algebra $H_v(n)$ over $A=\mathbb Z[v^{\pm1}]$ with
generators $T_1,\dots,T_{n-1}$, the quadratic relations
$(T_i-v)(T_i+1)=0$, the braid relations and the distant commutations, and with
$T_w$ the product of the $T_i$ along a reduced word for $w\in S_n$
([[def-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]]):

1. $\{T_w:w\in S_n\}$ is an $A$-basis of $H_v(n)$; in particular $H_v(n)$ is
free of rank $n!$ over $A$;
2. for every $w\in S_n$ and every $1\le i\le n-1$,
$$T_wT_i=T_{ws_i}\quad\text{if }\ell(ws_i)=\ell(w)+1,\qquad T_wT_i=(v-1)T_w+v\,T_{ws_i}\quad\text{if }\ell(ws_i)=\ell(w)-1,$$
where $\ell$ is the inversion length of $S_n$
([[def-weyl-group-and-length-for-finite-gl-n]]); consequently the rule rewrites
every monomial in the generators as an $A$-linear combination of the $T_w$.

No choice principle is used.

Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $q\in R^{\times}$, and $H=H_{R,q}(S_n)$ with
standard basis $\{T_w\}$ and star anti-automorphism $*$
([[def-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]],
[[thm-standard-basis-of-the-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]],
[[lem-the-star-antiautomorphism-of-the-type-a-hecke-algebra]]). For a
composition (in particular a partition) $\mu$ of $n$ put
$m_\mu:=\sum_{w\in S_\mu}T_w\in H$, the **row symmetrizer** of the standard
Young subgroup $S_\mu$
([[def-young-subgroup-tabloid-and-permutation-module]]); the sum has
$|S_\mu|=\prod_i\mu_i!$ terms.

For a row-standard $\mu$-tableau $s$
([[def-young-tableau-standard-tableau-and-shape]]) let $d(s)\in S_n$ be the
unique permutation with $s=t^{\mu}d(s)$, where $t^{\mu}$ is the row-standard
tableau obtained by entering $1,2,\dots,n$ in increasing order from left to
right along the rows: since $t^{\mu}$ is a fixed bijection from the nodes to
$\{1,\dots,n\}$, the permutation is the row-reading word of $s$,
$d(s)(p):=s(\text{the }p\text{-th node of }[\mu]\text{ in row-major order})$.
The stabiliser of $t^\mu$ is $S_\mu$ itself, because the row sets of $t^\mu$
are exactly the blocks of $\mu$
([[def-row-and-column-stabilizers-of-a-tableau]]). For row-standard tableau
$s$ one has $d(s)\in D_\mu$, the set of distinguished right-coset
representatives of $S_\mu$: $d(s)$ is the unique element of minimal length in
the coset $S_\mu d(s)$ with respect to the inversion length
([[def-weyl-group-and-length-for-finite-gl-n]]), and
$$\ell(wd)=\ell(w)+\ell(d)\qquad(w\in S_\mu,\ d\in D_\mu).$$
(This is the standard parabolic distinguished-representative property: since
the rows of $s$ are the blocks, $d(s)$ has no right descent $s_i$ with $i,i+1$
in the same block, and the exchange and deletion conditions of
[[lem-finite-weyl-strong-exchange-and-deletion]] upgrade this to the displayed
minimality and length additivity.)

For row-standard $\mu$-tableaux $s,t$ define the **Murphy element**
$$m_{st}:=T_{d(s)}^{*}\,m_{\mu}\,T_{d(t)}\in H,$$
and for a standard $\lambda$-tableau $t$ shorten
$m_t:=m_{tt}=T_{d(t)}^{*}m_\lambda T_{d(t)}$. Then $m_{st}^{*}=m_{ts}$ for all
row-standard $s,t$ of the same shape: applying the anti-automorphism, which
fixes $m_\mu$ because $m_\mu^*=\sum_{w\in S_\mu}T_{w^{-1}}=m_\mu$, gives
$$m_{st}^{*}=(T_{d(s)}^{*}m_\mu T_{d(t)})^{*}=T_{d(t)}^{*}m_\mu^{*}T_{d(s)}^{**}=T_{d(t)}^{*}m_\mu T_{d(s)}=m_{ts}.$$
Finally, $m_\mu T_w=q^{\ell(w)}m_\mu$ for every $w\in S_\mu$: it suffices to
prove this for $w=s_i$ a simple transposition with $i,i+1$ in the same block of
$\mu$, since any $w\in S_\mu\setminus\{1\}$ has a reduced expression
$w=w's_i$ with $\ell(w)=\ell(w')+1$ and the claim follows by induction,
$m_\mu T_w=m_\mu T_{w'}T_i=q^{\ell(w')}m_\mu T_i=q^{\ell(w)}m_\mu$. For such
$i$ the right multiplication $v\mapsto vs_i$ is an involution of the finite
group $S_\mu$, and pairing the summands of $m_\mu T_i=\sum_{v\in S_\mu}T_vT_i$
in twos gives, in the two cases of the standard-basis multiplication rule
$T_vT_i=T_{vs_i}$ if $\ell(vs_i)=\ell(v)+1$ and
$T_vT_i=(q-1)T_v+qT_{vs_i}$ if $\ell(vs_i)=\ell(v)-1$,
$$T_vT_i+T_{vs_i}T_i=q\,(T_v+T_{vs_i}),$$
so summing over the $\tfrac12|S_\mu|$ pairs yields $m_\mu T_i=qm_\mu$.

Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $q\in R^{\times}$, $H=H_{R,q}(S_n)$, and let
$L_1,\dots,L_n$ be the Hecke Jucys-Murphy elements
([[def-hecke-jucys-murphy-elements-and-q-contents]]). For every $\lambda\vdash n$,
every standard $\lambda$-tableau $t$ and every $1\le k\le n$ there exist
$a_v\in R$ with
$$m_tL_k=[\operatorname{content}_t(k)]_q\,m_t+\sum_{v\rhd t}a_v\,m_v,$$
where $(m_t)_{t\in\mathrm{Std}(\lambda)}$ is the Murphy basis of the Murphy cell
module $S^{\lambda}_{\mathrm M}$
([[def-type-a-hecke-specht-module-and-cell-form]]) and the sum is over standard
$\lambda$-tableaux $v$ strictly dominating $t$ in the dominance order on
tableaux ([[def-dominance-order-on-partitions]],
[[def-young-tableau-standard-tableau-and-shape]]). In particular $L_k$ acts on
the Murphy cell module $S^{\lambda}_{\mathrm M}$ with Murphy basis $(m_t)$ by a
triangular matrix whose diagonal entries are the q-content values.
Consequently the $L_k$ commute pairwise and every symmetric polynomial in
$L_1,\dots,L_n$ is central in $H$.

Let $A$ be a finite-dimensional cellular algebra over a field $F$
([[def-cellular-algebra-basis-and-cell-module]]) with cell modules
$C_\lambda$ and cell-form quotients $D_\lambda=C_\lambda/R_\lambda$. Then:

1. every nonzero $D_\lambda$ is an absolutely simple head, all simple
   $A$-modules occur exactly once this way, and $[C_\lambda:D_\mu]\ne0$ implies
   $\lambda\ge\mu$, with $[C_\mu:D_\mu]=1$ whenever $D_\mu\ne0$; here
   "nonzero quotient" means nonzero form, not necessarily a nondegenerate form
   on $C_\lambda$;
2. every nonzero cell module, including labels with zero-form quotient, has
   all its composition factors in a single block
   ([[def-blocks-of-a-finite-dimensional-algebra-by-primitive-central-idempotents]]);
3. two nonzero cell modules share a block exactly when they are linked by a
   finite chain of nonzero cell modules whose neighbouring terms share a
   simple composition factor;
4. for one primitive idempotent $e_\mu$ per simple,
   $$\dim_Fe_\mu Ae_\nu=\sum_\lambda[C_\lambda:D_\mu]\,[C_\lambda:D_\nu].$$

If the cellular index set $T(\lambda)$ is empty, then $C_\lambda=D_\lambda=0$.
Its block support, the set of primitive central idempotents $b$ with
$C_\lambda b\ne0$, is empty, and it has no simple composition factors.
It does not participate in the nonzero-cell linkage criterion of (3), and
its term in the corner sum of (4) is zero.

Let $\lambda,\mu\vdash n$ be partitions of the same integer $n$
([[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]]). We say that
$\lambda$ **dominates** $\mu$, and write $\lambda\unrhd\mu$, exactly when
$$\sum_{i=1}^{r}\lambda_i\;\ge\;\sum_{i=1}^{r}\mu_i\qquad\text{for every }r\ge1,$$
where each sequence is padded with zeros beyond its number of parts; since both
partitions have total $n$, both sides equal $n$ for all $r$ at least the number
of parts of either, so the condition is a finite family of inequalities between
integers. We write $\lambda\rhd\mu$ when $\lambda\unrhd\mu$ and
$\lambda\ne\mu$. The relation $\unrhd$ is the **dominance order** on the
partitions of $n$; we call $\lambda$ and $\mu$ **incomparable** when neither
$\lambda\unrhd\mu$ nor $\mu\unrhd\lambda$ holds.

Because it is defined by a family of non-strict inequalities between integers,
$\unrhd$ is reflexive and transitive. It is also antisymmetric: if
$\lambda\unrhd\mu$ and $\mu\unrhd\lambda$, then the prefix sums of $\lambda$ and
of $\mu$ are equal for every $r\ge1$, and subtracting consecutive prefix sums
gives $\lambda_i=\mu_i$ for every $i$ (both sequences are eventually zero).
Hence $\unrhd$ is a partial order on the set of partitions of $n$. For $n\ge1$,
the partition $(n)$ is its unique maximum and the partition $(1^n)$ its unique
minimum: for every $\mu\vdash n$ and every $r\ge1$ one has
$$\min(r,n)=\sum_{i\le r}(1^n)_i\;\le\;\sum_{i\le r}\mu_i\;\le\;n=\sum_{i\le r}(n)_i .$$

For $n=0$ the order is the trivial order on the one-element set
$\{\varnothing\}$.

Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $q\in R^\times$ and $\lambda\vdash n$, and let $C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda)$ with its basis $\{m_t\}$, $P(\lambda)=z_\lambda H$, the permutation form $\beta$ on $M(\lambda)$ and the DJ form on $P(\lambda)$ be as in [[def-dj-bridge-row-column-permutation-modules-and-polytabloids]], [[lem-dj-bridge-murphy-cellular-basis-and-cell-form]] and [[lem-dj-bridge-integral-murphy-and-polytabloid-straightening]]. Then:

1. Setting $B_\lambda(m_s,p):=\beta(x_\lambda T_{d_\lambda(s)},p)$ for $s\in\operatorname{Std}(\lambda)$ and $p\in P(\lambda)$ defines an explicit $R$-bilinear pairing $B_\lambda\colon C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda)\times P(\lambda)\to R$ that is $H$-balanced, $B_\lambda(mh,p)=B_\lambda(m,ph^*)$, and whose adjoint $c\mapsto B_\lambda(c,-)$ is an isomorphism of right $H$-modules $C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda)\to P(\lambda)^\circ$ onto the star-contragredient module of [[lem-dj-bridge-sign-automorphism-and-star-dual]]. No nondegeneracy of the DJ form $\beta_{P(\lambda)}$ is required.

2. Equivalently, the kernel of the quotient map $M(\lambda)\to C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda)$ is the orthogonal complement $P(\lambda)^\perp=\{a\in M(\lambda):\beta(a,p)=0\text{ for all }p\in P(\lambda)\}$, namely $M(\lambda)\cap I^{\rhd\lambda}$; the pairing matrices in the bases $\{m_s\}$ and $\{e_t\}$ have entries $B_\lambda(m_s,e_t)=q^{\ell(d_\lambda(s))}a_{d_\lambda(s),t}$ with $e_t=\sum_d a_{d,t}b_d$, and determinant a unit of $A=\mathbb Z[v^{\pm1}]$. Their inverses are finite tableau formulas given by the adjugate divided by this unit.

3. All statements are compatible with every base change $A\to R$, $v\mapsto q$; the construction uses no generic semisimplicity, no nondegeneracy of $\beta_{P(\lambda)}$ and no choice principle.

For every commutative ring $R$ and $q\in R^\times$:

1. $\theta(T_i):=(q-1)-T_i=-qT_i^{-1}$ extends uniquely to an involutive
$R$-algebra automorphism $\theta$ of $H=H_{R,q}(S_n)$, with
$\theta(T_w)=(-q)^{\ell(w)}T_{w^{-1}}^{-1}$; $\theta$ commutes with the star
anti-involution $*$ and is compatible with every base change.

2. For a right $H$-module $M$, the pullback $M^\theta$ (same underlying
$R$-module, action $m\cdot h:=m\theta(h)$) is a right $H$-module; $(-)^\theta$
is exact, preserves submodules, quotients, finite composition multiplicities and
simplicity, and $(M^\theta)^\theta=M$.

3. The star-contragredient $M^\circ:=\operatorname{Hom}_R(M,R)$ with
$(f\cdot h)(m):=f(mh^*)$ is a right $H$-module; for finite free $M$ it is finite
free of the same rank, $(-)^\circ$ commutes with base change, and
$(M^\theta)^\circ=(M^\circ)^\theta$.

4. For every partition $\lambda\vdash n$, if $w_0(S_\lambda)$ is the longest
element of the row subgroup, then
$$\theta(x_\lambda)=q^{\ell(w_0(S_\lambda))}y_\lambda,\qquad \theta(y_\lambda)=q^{-\ell(w_0(S_\lambda))}x_\lambda.$$
In particular $\theta(x_\lambda)$ and $y_\lambda$ differ by the unit
$q^{\ell(w_0(S_\lambda))}$, and this unit factor must be carried through every
form comparison. At $q=1$, $\theta$ is the pullback along the sign automorphism
$w\mapsto\operatorname{sgn}(w)w$ of $R[S_n]$.

No choice principle is used.

derivations.claim: The row-double-coset identity and membership. For a semistandard tableau $S$ of shape $\lambda$ and type $\rho$ and a standard $t$ of shape $\lambda$, every row-standard refinement $s$ of the column-strict tableau $S$ is standard, and $\sum_sT_{d(s)}^*x_\lambda$ is the sum of $T_w$ over the double coset $S_\rho d(s_0)^{-1}S_\lambda$, each $w$ occurring exactly once; its left $S_\rho$-coset expansion writes it as $x_\rho h_0$, and appending $T_{d(t)}$ gives $m_{(S,t)}=x_\rho h$ for some $h\in H_n$. Hence each $m_{(S,t)}$ lies in $x_\rho H_n$, and no row-intersection quantum factorial is introduced.

Independence and the Garnir coefficient rules. The sums $m_{(S,t)}$ are $R$-independent because their Murphy fibres (the index sets $\{s:ho(s)=S\}$) are disjoint and every coefficient in the expansion of $m_{(S,t)}$ in the $m_{st}$ basis is $1$; they therefore have disjoint unit pivots. For the coefficient rules, consider a violation at adjacent rows $i,i+1$ and column $j$ and the composition $
u=(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_{i-1},j-1,\lambda_i+1,\lambda_{i+1}-j,\lambda_{i+2},\dots)$; the two length-additive coset sums of $S_
u S_\lambda$ give $\sum_{w\in S_
u\cap D_\lambda}x_\lambda T_w =\sum_{v\in S_\lambda\cap D_
u}T_v^*x_
u,$ whose distinguished Garnir term occurs with coefficient $1$. Every other term in the original shape has strictly more dominant row tableaux, the reordered $
u$ has strictly higher lexicographic shape, and the ordinary Murphy dominance refinement places these shape errors in higher-cell ideals; a nonstandard tableau factors as that Garnir tableau followed by an additive-length word (removing inversions while keeping the column violation), and Bruhat subword support preserves the strict tableau-prefix inequality. In the isolated relation for consecutive $a,a+1$ in one column, sorting the Garnir belt has a unique standard term whose single adjacent swap produces the distinguished Garnir term, with coefficient $-1$, and every other same-shape term is strictly more dominant. This yields the displayed congruence of the Statement, and the right analogue follows by the cellular involutions $*$.

The row eigenspace test. For a fixed $a$ the left $z$-eigenspace of $T_a$ in $H_n$ is $(1+T_a)H_n$: in the $T_w$ basis pair $w$ with $s_aw$ of larger length, and coefficient comparison in $T_ah=zh$ gives equality of the two coefficients, whose sum is $(1+T_a)T_w$. This argument uses only that $z$ is a unit. Over the universal domain, no element of this space has a nonzero Murphy coefficient at a tableau with $a,a+1$ in one column: choose a least shape and then a least left tableau in a dominance-compatible support order; higher-cell terms cannot contribute to its shape, and a column correction from another tableau can contribute only from a strictly less dominant left tableau, absent by minimality. Symmetric polynomials are central. Since the coefficients of distinct permutations are independent, the invariant subspace has the orbit sums of nontrivial colored cycles as a basis, with no averaging: a coefficient constant on its orbit needs no division by $n!$. For $m\le\ell$ every lower exponent in $J_m$ is below $\ell$, so $E_n(J_m)=0$; likewise $E_n(X_n^mU)=0$ for $1\le m<\ell$. Every component-preserving row-standard multitableau factors its distinguished permutation into a permutation inside the contiguous component intervals followed by the unique shuffle of the intervals preserving internal order; the two inversion sets are disjoint, so the factorization is length-additive. Multiplying by $u_\lambda$ (which commutes with the Hecke generators internal to the intervals), ordinary Murphy straightening applies in each component; higher ordinary component shapes preserve component sizes and strictly increase multipartition dominance, and the final component shuffle relabels each component by an increasing list whose selected entries at any cutoff are an initial segment, so tableau-prefix inequalities are exactly the ordinary ones at the corresponding initial-segment length. For a fixed initial left row and right multiplication by $T_i$: if $ts_i$ is standard the length formula gives the usual standard term (or $q_H$ times it plus $(q_H-1)m_{t^\lambda t}$); if $i,i+1$ share a row the result is $q_Hm$; and if they share a component but the interchange fails standardness, factoring out the increasing component shuffle and applying the ordinary cell law gives same-shape terms with the same initial left row and strictly higher multipartition terms, the required transfer identity $T_cT_i=T_jT_c$ following from $cs_i=s_jc$ and the length/quadratic formula. A cross-component column failure is impossible because column standardness is imposed componentwise. Descending induction over a linear extension of multipartition dominance therefore makes each $N^{\ge\lambda}$ and $N^{>\lambda}$ stable under all finite generators; multiplying on the left by $T_{d(s)}^*$ and applying $*$ makes the higher spans two-sided ideals. This induction concerns spanning sets only and assumes no independence. [F1, algebra]

The cyclotomic component shift. Let $a=(a_k)$ with $a_k=\sum_{b<k}|\lambda^{(b)}|$ and $u_a=u_\lambda$, and let $b=a+e_k$. Put $u_b=u_a(X_{a_k+1}-Q_k)$; the factors commute, and for $a=a_k$ the defining recurrence gives the exact identity $u_aT_a\cdots T_1X_1T_1\cdots T_a=q_H^a igl(Q_ku_a+u_b igr),$ by substituting $T_a\cdots T_1X_1T_1\cdots T_a=q_H^aX_{a+1}$ and adding/subtracting $Q_ku_a$; the case $a=0$ is included. For $k>1$ form the multicomposition $
u$ obtained by appending a singleton row to component $k-1$ and deleting the first node of the first row of component $k$. Its cumulative sizes are $b$, so $u_
u=u_b$, and its Young subgroup is contained in $S_\lambda$; the left length-additive coset expansion gives $x_\lambda u_b=\sum_vT_v^*m_
u$. Sorting the rows of $
u$ in each component conjugates its Young subgroup and gives $m_
u=T_dm_{\operatorname{sort}
u}T_d^{-1}$ with $u_
u$ commuting with the component-preserving permutation, so the ordinary row-sorting argument expresses each term in standard pairs of shapes at least $\operatorname{sort}
u$, which strictly dominates $\lambda$: the cumulative total through component $k-1$ strictly increases and no later cumulative sum decreases. Hence $x_\lambda u_b\in N^{>\lambda}$. For $k=1$, nonemptiness of component $1$ forces $a_s\ge1$ for all $s\ge2$, so $u_b$ contains every factor $(X_1-Q_s)$ and vanishes by the cyclotomic relation; again $x_\lambda u_b\in N^{>\lambda}$. Right multiplication by $X_1$. Let $t$ be standard with entry $1$ in component $k$, an initial node, and initial label $a+1$ with $a=a_k$. Then $d(t)=(s_a\cdots s_1)w$ with $w$ fixing $1$ and $\ell(d(t))=a+\ell(w)$: pulling label $a+1$ to value $1$ crosses exactly the $a$ smaller initial labels, whose final values exceed $1$. A permutation fixing $1$ has a reduced word in $s_2,\dots,s_{n-1}$, so $T_w$ commutes with $X_1$. Multiplying the identity of step 1.2 on the right by $(T_1\cdots T_a)^{-1}$ and then by $T_w$ gives $m_\lambda T_{d(t)}X_1=q_H^aQ_km_\lambda(T_1\cdots T_a)^{-1}T_w +q_H^ax_\lambda u_b(T_1\cdots T_a)^{-1}T_w,$ whose second term lies in $N^{>\lambda}$ by step 1.2 and finite-generator stability, and whose first term lies modulo $N^{>\lambda}$ in the fixed-initial-row span. Hence that span is stable under $X_1$; multiplying on the left by $T_{d(s)}^*$ and using the left stability of the higher shapes gives the coefficient-independence law $m_{st}h\equiv\sum_vr_{(t,v)}(h)m_{sv}\pmod{N^{>\lambda}}$ first for each generator and then for every word, with coefficients independent of $s$, and $*$ makes the higher spans two-sided. Since $X_r=q_H^{1-r}T_{r-1}\cdots T_1X_1T_1\cdots T_{r-1}$ and the cyclotomic constant term is a unit when the $Q_a$ are invertible, these generators generate the Laurent affine quotient. Spanning and cellularity. The smallest multipartition $\omega=(\varnothing,\dots,\varnothing,(1^n))$ satisfies $u_\omega=x_\omega=m_\omega=1$, so the generator-stable span of the standard $m_{st}$ contains $1$ and is all of $H_n$: the Murphy family spans. Every commutative specialization with unit parameters inherits the basis and the cell law. No primitive-block classification is used. [step 2.1, step 3.1] ∎

For $H_n$ in
[[def-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-cell-and-schur-modules]] over
the universal Laurent parameter ring, the elements $m_{st}$ indexed by all
$\ell$-multipartitions of $n$ and standard tableaux $s,t$ of that shape are a
basis and a dominance-cellular datum:
$$m_{st}^*=m_{ts},\qquad m_{st}h\equiv\sum_vr_{(t,v)}(h)\,m_{sv}\pmod{H^{>\lambda}},$$
with coefficients $r_{(t,v)}(h)$ independent of $s$. The higher spans are
actual two-sided ideals. Every commutative specialization with unit parameters
inherits the cellular basis; in particular the arbitrary-field finite-$e$
charged specializations and the LM deformation DVR retain it. The universal
rank is supplied independently by
[[lem-universal-cyclotomic-hecke-ordered-monomials-form-a-basis]], not by a
primitive-block classification.

Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $n\ge0$ and $\ell\ge1$, and let $z,U_1,\dots,U_\ell$
be units of $R$ ([[def-algebra-over-a-commutative-ring]]). The **arbitrary-level
cyclotomic Hecke algebra** $H_n=H_n(R;z;U_1,\dots,U_\ell)$ is the $R$-algebra
presented by invertible commuting elements $X_1,\dots,X_n$ and generators
$T_1,\dots,T_{n-1}$ subject to the relations
$$(T_i-z)(T_i+1)=0,\qquad T_iT_{i+1}T_i=T_{i+1}T_iT_{i+1},\qquad T_iT_j=T_jT_i\quad(|i-j|>1),$$
$$T_iX_iT_i=zX_{i+1},\qquad X_jT_i=T_iX_j\quad(j\notin\{i,i+1\}),\qquad \prod_{a=1}^{\ell}(X_1-U_a)=0 .$$
For $n=0$ set $H_0=R$. The **grading variable** of this page is $v$, not the
unit $z$: the two are identified only where a statement says so explicitly.

**Multipartitions and Murphy data.** An $\ell$-**multipartition** of $n$ is an
ordered tuple $\lambda=(\lambda^{(1)},\dots,\lambda^{(\ell)})$ of partitions
with $\sum_{b}|\lambda^{(b)}|=n$ ([[def-young-tableau-standard-tableau-and-shape]]).
Multipartitions are partially ordered by dominance, $\lambda\unrhd\mu$ meaning
that $\sum_{b\le k}|\lambda^{(b)}|+\sum_{j\le m}\lambda^{(k)}_j\ge
\sum_{b\le k}|\mu^{(b)}|+\sum_{j\le m}\mu^{(k)}_j$ for all $k,m$. Fill the
diagram $t^\lambda$ with $1,\dots,n$ in component order, then row order, then
column order. Put $a_k:=\sum_{b<k}|\lambda^{(b)}|$,
$u_\lambda:=\prod_{k=1}^{\ell}\prod_{j\le a_k}(X_j-U_k)$,
$x_\lambda:=\sum_{w\in S_\lambda}T_w$, and $m_\lambda:=x_\lambda u_\lambda$,
where $S_\lambda$ is the row subgroup: the subgroup of $S_n$ stabilizing the
rows of $t^\lambda$
([[def-finite-symmetric-group-and-permutation-notation]],
[[def-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]]). Write $M_\lambda:=m_\lambda H_n$ for
the right $H_n$-submodule generated by $m_\lambda$
([[def-left-and-right-modules]]). The **presentation involution** $*$ of $H_n$
fixes every $X_j$ and every $T_i$ and reverses products. For standard
tableaux $s,t$ of shape $\lambda$ put $m_{st}:=T_{d(s)}^{*}m_\lambda T_{d(t)}$,
where $d(s)$ is the permutation determined by $t^\lambda d(s)=s$.
Denote by $H^{>\lambda}$ the span of the higher Murphy shapes once their
basis and cell law is established by
[[thm-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-basis-is-cellular]], and by
$S_\lambda$ the right cell (**Specht**) module with basis $m_t$ and the
action given by that cell law; its cellular form defines
$D_\lambda:=S_\lambda/\operatorname{rad}S_\lambda$, which may vanish.

**Types.** The types used below are **exactly** all $\ell$-multipartitions of
$n$, including tuples with empty components — not all multicompositions. A
**semistandard tableau** $S$ has entries the labels $(i,k)$ (row $i$ in
component $k$) ordered by component first and then by row, weakly increasing
along rows, strictly increasing down columns, and a label of component $a$
may occur only in physical component $b\le a$
([[def-semistandard-tableau-and-kostka-number]]); the **type** of $S$ is the
multipartition counting each label with the multiplicity of the corresponding
row. For standard $s$ let $\mu(s)$ be the tableau obtained from $s$ by
replacing each entry by its row-and-component in $t^{\mu}$. Put
$$m_{(S,t)}:=\sum_{s:\,\mu(s)=S}m_{st},\qquad m_{(S,T)}:=\sum_{s,t:\,\mu(s)=S,\ \nu(t)=T}m_{st}.$$
Let
$$M:=\bigoplus_{\lambda\ \text{multipartition of}\ n}M_\lambda,\qquad C_n:=\operatorname{End}_{H_n}(M),$$
with ordinary composition ([[def-direct-sum-of-a-family-of-modules]]). For
$S,T$ of shape $\lambda$ and types $\mu,\nu$, the map $\varphi_{ST}$ — once
justified by [[lem-cyclotomic-semistandard-sums-give-schur-endomorphism-basis]] —
sends $m_\alpha h$ to $\delta_{\alpha,\nu}m_{(S,T)}h$. Its right cell module
$\Delta_\lambda$ has basis $v_T$ over the semistandard $T$ of multipartition
types, with contravariant cell form and quotient $L_\lambda$. Let $T^\lambda$
be the unique tableau of shape and type $\lambda$, and let $e_\lambda$ be the
identity projection onto $M_\lambda$. Put $\omega:=(\varnothing,\dots,\varnothing,(1^n))$
and $e:=e_\omega$; then $m_\omega=1$, so $M_\omega=H_n$, and $H_n$ is an
actual direct summand of $M$. The weight projections used by the Jantzen
theory below are the $e_\nu$ with $\nu$ a multipartition. Write
$K_{(\lambda,\nu)}:=\#\operatorname{SStd}_\nu(\lambda)$ for the number of
semistandard tableaux of shape $\lambda$ and type $\nu$.

**Boundary of the definition.** All asserted module, form and map laws are
discharged by the linked local suppliers
[[thm-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-basis-is-cellular]],
[[lem-cyclotomic-semistandard-sums-give-schur-endomorphism-basis]] and
[[thm-cyclotomic-schur-standards-and-schur-functor-control-block-linkage]];
the definition itself claims no proof of them and no primitive
residue-content classification. No choice principle is used: only finite
bases, finite subgroup and coset decompositions, finite filtrations and
explicit polynomial identities occur.

Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $q\in R^{\times}$, $H=H_{R,q}(S_n)$, and let
$L_1,\dots,L_n$ be the Hecke Jucys-Murphy elements
([[def-hecke-jucys-murphy-elements-and-q-contents]]). For every $\lambda\vdash n$,
every standard $\lambda$-tableau $t$ and every $1\le k\le n$ there exist
$a_v\in R$ with
$$m_tL_k=[\operatorname{content}_t(k)]_q\,m_t+\sum_{v\rhd t}a_v\,m_v,$$
where $(m_t)_{t\in\mathrm{Std}(\lambda)}$ is the Murphy basis of the Murphy cell
module $S^{\lambda}_{\mathrm M}$
([[def-type-a-hecke-specht-module-and-cell-form]]) and the sum is over standard
$\lambda$-tableaux $v$ strictly dominating $t$ in the dominance order on
tableaux ([[def-dominance-order-on-partitions]],
[[def-young-tableau-standard-tableau-and-shape]]). In particular $L_k$ acts on
the Murphy cell module $S^{\lambda}_{\mathrm M}$ with Murphy basis $(m_t)$ by a
triangular matrix whose diagonal entries are the q-content values.
Consequently the $L_k$ commute pairwise and every symmetric polynomial in
$L_1,\dots,L_n$ is central in $H$.

derivations.claim: Initial-row eigenvalues. For component $k$ and $a=a_k$, [F1] gives $m_\lambda(X_{a+1}-Q_k)=x_\lambda u_b\in N^{>\lambda}$. The internal finite Hecke submodule generated by $m_\lambda$ modulo higher global shapes is spanned by standard internal component permutations; each such permutation fixes the smallest internal label $a+1$ (that label occupies the first node of its component), so its Hecke element has a reduced word in the internal generators with indices at least $a+2$ and commutes with $X_{a+1}$. Hence $X_{a+1}$ acts as the scalar $Q_k$ on that whole submodule, with errors in the two-sided ideal $N^{>\lambda}$. The $X$-recurrence then identifies $X_{a+i}$ on this submodule with $Q_k$ times the ordinary multiplicative Jucys–Murphy element $M_i$ of [F2], by induction from the finite quadratic relation and the additive-JM recurrence (a polynomial identity also at $q_H=1$). Ordinary JM triangularity gives diagonal $Q_kq_H^{c-r}$ at the node $(r,c,k)$ occupied by local entry $i$: the internal label $i$ is not a row index, and no extra subtraction of $i-1$ occurs. For the initial component tableau, which is maximal in tableau dominance, there are no strictly more dominant same-shape terms. Thus for the node $(r,c,k)$ carrying global entry $t$, $m_\lambda X_t\equiv Q_kq_H^{c-r}m_\lambda\pmod{N^{>\lambda}}$.

JM triangularity for every standard multitableau. Inducting through a reduced word of $w$, the relations [F1] give $T_wX_r=X_{w^{-1}(r)}T_w+\sum_{v<w}\sum_ba_{(v,b)}X_bT_v,$ where the corrections are supported on proper Bruhat subwords (at the first correction a generator is deleted, moving its linear $X$-coefficient through preceding generators deletes further generators, and finite quadratic multiplication preserves Bruhat support). Applying this with $w=d(t)$ and multiplying by $m_\lambda$ on the left, step 1.1 evaluates every surviving $X$ coefficient modulo higher shapes; a correction $m_\lambda T_v$ reduces first to a row-standard representative $d(u)$ of its Young-subgroup coset, the removed row subgroup contributing its row eigenvalue, with $d(u)\le v<d(t)$; the Bruhat/tableau-prefix relation on the ordered rows of all components then makes $u$ strictly dominate $t$, and componentwise straightening of $u$ keeps the shape or produces same-shape tableaux at least $u$ in prefix dominance, hence strictly dominating $t$. The leading eigenvalue is $Q_kq_H^{j-i}$ at the node carrying $r$, because $w^{-1}(r)$ is its initial-row label. Therefore $m_{(t^\lambda,t)}X_r\equiv Q_kq_H^{j-i}m_{(t^\lambda,t)} +\sum_{v\lhd t}a_vm_{(t^\lambda,v)}\pmod{N^{>\lambda}},$ the exact arbitrary-level JM content statement, independent of an affine center theorem, semisimplicity or block classification.

Residue words and boundary cases. On the resulting Specht module a total ordering extending tableau dominance triangularizes all the $X_r$ simultaneously; the one-dimensional successive quotients have exactly the content characters of step 2.1, so every simultaneous generalized eigenword is among the standard-tableau residue words $c_a+j-i\pmod e$ ([[thm-hecke-jucys-murphy-action-is-dominance-triangular]] for the ordinary part); the residue multiplicities of every such word equal the node-residue multiplicities of $\lambda$, since permuting the labels of a standard tableau does not change the multiset of node residues. For rank zero, $H=F$, the sole shape and tableau are empty and all assertions have their one-dimensional interpretation. The triangularity is polynomial in the parameters, so it specializes to the LM deformation DVR and to the generic fibre.

For every commutative ring $R$ with invertible parameter $z$, the ordinary finite type-A Hecke algebra $H_n$ and a composition $\rho$ of $n$, the permutation module $x_\rho H_n$ has $R$-basis $$m_{(S,t)}=\sum_{s:\,\rho(s)=S}m_{st},$$ where $S$ ranges over the semistandard tableaux of partition shape and type $\rho$ and $t$ over the standard tableaux of the same shape.

For $n\ge2$, the symmetric group $S_n$ has the presentation $$S_n=\langle s_1,\dots,s_{n-1}\mid s_i^2=1,\ s_is_{i+1}s_i=s_{i+1}s_is_{i+1},\ s_is_j=s_js_i\ (|i-j|>1)\rangle,$$ where, after relabelling the underlying set $n=\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ as $\{1,\ldots,n\}$, $s_i$ corresponds to the adjacent transposition $(i\ i+1)$.

Let $A$ be a finite-dimensional cellular algebra over a field $F$
([[def-cellular-algebra-basis-and-cell-module]]) with cell modules
$C_\lambda$ and cell-form quotients $D_\lambda=C_\lambda/R_\lambda$. Then:

1. every nonzero $D_\lambda$ is an absolutely simple head, all simple
   $A$-modules occur exactly once this way, and $[C_\lambda:D_\mu]\ne0$ implies
   $\lambda\ge\mu$, with $[C_\mu:D_\mu]=1$ whenever $D_\mu\ne0$; here
   "nonzero quotient" means nonzero form, not necessarily a nondegenerate form
   on $C_\lambda$;
2. every nonzero cell module, including labels with zero-form quotient, has
   all its composition factors in a single block
   ([[def-blocks-of-a-finite-dimensional-algebra-by-primitive-central-idempotents]]);
3. two nonzero cell modules share a block exactly when they are linked by a
   finite chain of nonzero cell modules whose neighbouring terms share a
   simple composition factor;
4. for one primitive idempotent $e_\mu$ per simple,
   $$\dim_Fe_\mu Ae_\nu=\sum_\lambda[C_\lambda:D_\mu]\,[C_\lambda:D_\nu].$$

If the cellular index set $T(\lambda)$ is empty, then $C_\lambda=D_\lambda=0$.
Its block support, the set of primitive central idempotents $b$ with
$C_\lambda b\ne0$, is empty, and it has no simple composition factors.
It does not participate in the nonzero-cell linkage criterion of (3), and
its term in the corner sum of (4) is zero.

On the Specht module $S_\lambda$ of [[def-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-cell-and-schur-modules]], $X_r$ acts dominance-triangularly with diagonal $U_az^{j-i}$ at the node $(i,j,a)$ carrying $r$.

derivations.claim: The affine expansion with only variable-difference denominators. Writing $T_w$ as the product of the $\Phi_i$ and the scalars $c_{i,i+1}$ along a reduced word of $w$ and moving a Laurent polynomial $f$ leftward across the $\Phi$'s by [F2] expresses $T_wf$ as a sum of terms $c_v\,v(f)$ times a monomial in a subword, where $v$ runs over products of subwords of that reduced word, every denominator of $c_v$ is a product of differences $X_i-X_j$, and each $v$ is Bruhat-below $w$ by the subword characterization of Bruhat order ([F6]). In particular applying this with $f=u_\lambda$ keeps all denominators among the variable differences and introduces no $U_a-U_b$, quantum factorial, or Gram determinant. [F1, F2, F6, algebra]

Flagging is Bruhat-downward closed and gives monic divisibility. Let $S$ be semistandard of shape $\lambda$ and type $\mu$, and for a permutation $\sigma$ let $\pi=\sigma^{-1}$ map each label to its physical position; set $A_k=|\lambda^{(1)}|+\cdots+|\lambda^{(k)}|$ and $B_k=|\mu^{(1)}|+\cdots+|\mu^{(k)}|$. Then $eCe=\operatorname{End}_H(H)\cong H$ by left multiplication, and $Ce\cong\operatorname{Hom}_H(H,M)\cong M$ by evaluation at $1$. If $c\in Z(C)$, then $c$ restricts on the $H$-summand to left multiplication by some $h$; for each $m\in M$ the $H$-map $f_m:H\to M$, $a\mapsto ma$, is the off-diagonal block $j f_m\pi\in C$ through $H$, and commuting it with $c$ and evaluating at $1$ gives $c(m)=mh$. Since $c$ is $H$-linear, $c(ab)=c(a)b$ for $a,b\in H$ gives $ab h=ahb$, so with $a=1$ we get $hb=bh$ and $h\in Z(H)$. Conversely every $h\in Z(H)$ defines the $H$-linear endomorphism $m\mapsto mh$, which commutes with every $H$-endomorphism of $M$, hence is central in $C$. These constructions are inverse unital algebra maps, so $Z(C)\cong Z(H)$ and primitive central idempotents correspond bijectively ([F4]). Split quasiheredity by an explicit heredity chain. Order the multipartitions in a linear extension of dominance and remove the maximal remaining cell layers successively; in the relevant quotient algebra $B$ the next layer $J$ has basis $c_{st}$ with a distinguished index $u$ whose Gram value is $G(u,u)=1$. Then $e=c_{uu}$ is idempotent, $c_{su}c_{ut}=c_{st}$, and the multiplication map $Be\otimes_FeB\to J$ is an isomorphism on these basis elements; also $eBe=Fe$, since the cell law and maximality of $J$ show every $ebe$ is a scalar multiple of $e$. Hence $Be$ is projective, $J$ is a direct sum of copies of $Be$, and $e\,\mathrm{rad}(B)\,e=0$ because the corner is a field. Thus $J$ is a split heredity ideal, and iterating gives a split heredity chain whose standards are the cell modules $\Delta_\lambda$; so $C_n$ is split quasihereditary over $F$. [F2, F3, algebra]

derivations.claim: Word separation over the universal fraction field. Assign to each standard multitableau the sequence of joint Jucys–Murphy words: the diagonal values $U_az^{j-i}$ at the nodes carrying the labels $1,\dots,n$ ([F3]). If two standard multitableaux first differ at step $r$, then their restrictions to the boxes $1,\dots,r-1$ coincide, and the two added nodes are two different addable nodes of that common prefix shape. If the two nodes lie in one physical component, their contents $j-i$ are different (two addable nodes of a partition have different contents), and $z$ is transcendental over the base field, so $z^{j-i}\ne z^{j'-i'}$. If they lie in different components $a\ne b$, the values $U_az^{j-i}$ and $U_bz^{j'-i'}$ are distinct in $K$, because $z,U_1,\dots,U_\ell$ are algebraically independent monomials and the components differ. Hence the joint word determines the tableau, different standard multitableaux -- even of different shapes -- have different joint words, and distinct shapes have disjoint sets of word characters. [F1, F3, algebra]

Generic simplicity and split semisimplicity. By [F3] each $S_\lambda$ has a simultaneous triangular filtration whose successive characters are its own words of step 1.1. Hence every composition factor $D_\mu$ of the nonzero module $S_\lambda$ has a word occurring in $S_\mu$ and a word occurring in $S_\lambda$; disjointness of shape word sets forces $\mu=\lambda$. In particular $D_\lambda\ne0$, and the cellular diagonal multiplicity $[S_\lambda:D_\lambda]=1$ of [F4] forces $S_\lambda=D_\lambda$ to be simple, with the distinct absolutely simple modules $S_\lambda$ as the only composition factors. The cellular basis exhibits $H_K$ as a right module direct sum of $\dim_K S_\lambda$ copies of $S_\lambda$ over all $\lambda$ ([F2]), so all composition factors of $H_K$ are simple and $\sum_\lambda(\dim_K S_\lambda)^2=\dim_K H_K$; therefore $\mathrm{rad}\,H_K=0$ and $H_K$ is split semisimple. [F2, F3, F4, step 1.1, algebra]

Word separation for the Lyle–Mathas deformation. Fix $N\ge1$, nonzero $q_H,Q_a$ in $F$, and set $z=q_Ht$, $U_a=Q_at^{Na}$ in $F(t)$. For two standard multitableaux that first differ at a step $r\le N$, the common prefix of size $r-1$ has components of sizes summing to $r-1$; the two added nodes lie in components $a,b$ and each added content $c=j-i$ is bounded in absolute value by the size of its own component, so $|c-c'|<r\le N$. A collision $U_az^c=U_bz^{c'}$ with $a\ne b$ would force the equality $Na+c=Nb+c'$ of $t$-adic exponents, i.e. the nonzero multiple $N(a-b)$ of $N$ would equal $c'-c$ with $|c'-c|<N$, impossible. If $a=b$, then $z$ is transcendental over $F$, so $z^c=z^{c'}$ forces $c=c'$. Thus the joint words separate all rank-$d$ standards in $F(t)$ as in step 1.1, and the argument of step 2.1 proves that the rank-$d$ Specht modules are simple and the corresponding Hecke algebra is split semisimple over $F(t)$, with no affine-center or block-classification input. [F1, F3, step 1.1, algebra]

Nondegenerate Schur standards. By [F6], over any field with unit parameters, $[\Delta_\lambda:L_\mu]=[S_\lambda:D_\mu]$ whenever $D_\mu\ne0$, and every $\Delta_\lambda$ is nonzero. Over $K$, step 2.1 makes every $S_\lambda$ simple; hence $D_\mu=0$ never occurs, $[\Delta_\lambda:L_\lambda]=[S_\lambda:S_\lambda]=1$, and since all $L_\mu$ are distinct the multiplicity list forces $\Delta_\lambda=L_\lambda$ to be simple; the diagonal cell-form entry of the standard of shape and type $\lambda$ is $1$, so the cellular form is nonzero and, being invariant on a simple module, is nondegenerate. The same argument applies over $F(t)$ to the rank-$d$ standards using step 3.1, and the construction of [F5] and the multiplicities of [F6] are identities over the respective ground fields, so the charged finite-$e$ specializations used by the Lyle–Mathas deformation are included. No valuation of a weight-Gram determinant is computed. [F5, F6, step 2.1, step 3.1, algebra] ∎

u u_T}= rac{\gamma_{t_T}}{c_Tu_T},$ and the off-diagonal entries vanish, so $\det G_{\lambda
u}=\prod_{T\in\operatorname{SStd}_
u(\lambda)} rac{\gamma_{t_T}}{c_Tu_T}.$ [step 2.1, step 2.2, step 3.1, step 3.2, algebra]

The explicit symmetrizer value of $c_T$. In the rational crossed product [F2], for a row interval $I$ and $x_I=\sum_{w\in S_I}T_w$, write $x_I=\sum_wa_ww$; the row-coset identity $T_ix_I=zx_I$ gives $a_{s_iw}=s_i(a_w)$ by coefficient comparison with $T_i=c_{i,i+1}+d_{i,i+1}s_i$, and the coefficient of the longest permutation comes from the product of the $d_{ij}=(X_j-zX_i)/(X_j-X_i)$ over the positive roots of $I$, each once. Hence $a_1=w_0 igl(\prod_{i<j\in I} rac{X_j-zX_i}{X_j-X_i} igr)=\prod_{i<j\in I} rac{zX_j-X_i}{X_j-X_i}=C_I(X)$. Disjoint row intervals commute, so $x_
u=\prod_Ix_I$ has identity coefficient $\prod_IC_I(X)$; expanding $x_I=C_I(X)+\sum_{w
e1}b_w(X)\Phi_w$ and using that every $\Phi_w$ with $w
e1$ changes the distinct row entries and hence the JM word, the diagonal coefficient of $f_{t_T}x_
u$ is exactly $C_{t_T}$ evaluated at the residues of $t_T$. Therefore $c_T=C_{t_T}=\prod_{i<j\ 	ext{same type row}} rac{zr_{t_T}(j)-r_{t_T}(i)}{r_{t_T}(j)-r_{t_T}(i)}$. Every factor is nonzero in the stated generic fields: in one physical component two nodes of a horizontal strip have distinct contents, and in the deformation two nodes of different components have content difference at most $n-2$, which cannot cancel the exponent $n(a-b)$. [F2, F3, step 3.2, algebra]

The inversion-set formula and the explicit product. Every standard tableau is a linear extension of the node order; bubble-sorting it toward the initial extension swaps adjacent inverted (hence incomparable) nodes exactly once and never swaps comparable ones, so reversing those swaps and multiplying the recurrence of step 3.3 gives $\gamma_{t_T}=\gamma_{t^\lambda}\prod_{\substack{x<y\\t_T(x)>t_T(y)}}R(r_x,r_y),$ and $R$ is symmetric in its arguments. Dividing by $C_{t_T}$ and $u_T$ and using $\gamma_{t^\lambda}/u_T=P_\lambda(z)B_T$ with $B_T=\prod_x\prod_{a(x)<b\le a_T(x)}(r_x-U_b)$ (a literal nested-product cancellation by the flag condition), together with the telescoping row identity $\prod_{i<j}C(A_i,A_j)=[r]_z!$ for residues $A_j=A_1z^{j-1}$ in a row of length $r$, the four pair classes — same physical row with same or different labels, different physical rows with same or different labels — give exactly $\frac{\gamma_{t_T}}{C_{t_T}u_T}=B_T\prod_{(x,y)\in\mathcal C(T)}C(r_x,r_y)\prod_{(x,y)\in\mathcal I(T)}R(r_x,r_y),$ where $\mathcal C(T)$ collects pairs $x<y$ that are in one physical row with different labels or in different physical rows with the same label, and $\mathcal I(T)$ collects pairs $x<y$ in different physical rows with $L_T(x)>L_T(y)$. Multiplying over $T$ and collecting like node pairs yields $\det G_{\lambda\nu}=\prod_TB_T\prod_{x<y}C(r_x,r_y)^{c_{xy}}R(r_x,r_y)^{i_{xy}},\qquad c_{xy}=\#\{T:(x,y)\in\mathcal C(T)\},\qquad i_{xy}=\#\{T:(x,y)\in\mathcal I(T)\}.$ All factors are nonzero in the two generic regimes by step 4.2, the empty weight contributes determinant $1$, and no factor $P_\nu$ or $c_T$ is inverted in the $\mathcal O$-lattice; this proves both displayed determinant formulas. [F1, step 4.1, step 3.3, step 4.2, algebra] ∎

citations.quote: Work with the arbitrary-level Murphy/Schur datum of [[def-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-cell-and-schur-modules]] over either (i) the fraction field $K$ of the universal Laurent parameter ring, including the generic field of the Lyle–Mathas deformation, or (ii) any field $F$ with nonzero $q_H,Q_1,\dots,Q_\ell$ under the deformation $z=q_Ht$, $U_a=Q_at^{na}$ in $F(t)$.

Let $F$ be a field, let $F[t,t^{-1}]$ be its Laurent polynomial ring ([[def-the-laurent-polynomial-ring]]), and let $v_1$ be the $(t-1)$-adic valuation on the nonzero elements of $F[t,t^{-1}]$: for $0\ne f$, $$v_1(f):=\max\{n\ge0:(t-1)^n\mid f\ \text{in}\ F[t,t^{-1}]\},$$ so that $v_1(f)=0$ exactly when $f(1)\ne0$ ([[def-discrete-valuation-ring]]).
Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $n\ge0$ and $\ell\ge1$, and let $z,U_1,\dots,U_\ell$ be units of $R$ ([[def-algebra-over-a-commutative-ring]]).

Let $\lambda\vdash n$ and let $[\lambda]$ be its Young diagram ([[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]]). A **tableau of shape $\lambda$**, or $\lambda$-tableau, is a bijection $$t:[\lambda]\longrightarrow\{1,2,\dots,n\}.$$ We write $t(i,j)$ for the entry of $t$ in the node $(i,j)$, and we display $t$ as the diagram $[\lambda]$ with each node carrying its entry.

Let $\lambda\vdash n$ and $\mu\vdash n$ be partitions of the same integer $n$, with diagrams $[\lambda]$ and $[\mu]$ ([[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]]). For content counts only, set $\mu_i:=0$ for $i$ beyond the number of parts of $\mu$; these zeros are not additional parts of the partition.

Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $n\ge1$, and let $A=(a_{ij})\in M_n(R)$. Its **determinant** is $$\det(A):=\sum_{\sigma\in S_n}\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)\prod_{i<n}a_{\sigma(i),i}.$$ The sum is finite because $S_n$ has $n!$ elements. The product is taken in $R$, so the signs $1$ and $-1$ act through the ring identities. The formula uses columns indexed by $i<n$ and rows indexed by $\sigma(i)$.

derivations.claim: Characters as finite symmetric polynomials. Fix $d\ge n$ row labels per type component with ordered variables $x_{(a,r)}$, put $Y_a=\{x_{(b,r)}:b\ge a\}$ with the inherited order, and for a shape $\lambda$ let $\operatorname{ch}_\lambda(x)=\sum_{T\in\operatorname{SStd}(\lambda)}x^{\operatorname{wt}(T)}$. The flag condition says that the physical component $a$ of a semistandard tableau is an ordinary semistandard tableau over the alphabet $Y_a$, and the components are chosen independently, so $\operatorname{ch}_\lambda(x)=\prod_a s_{\lambda^{(a)}}(Y_a)$ with $s_\rho(Y)=\det(h_{\rho_i-i+j}(Y))$. The determinant equals the ordinary semistandard generating polynomial: expand it as signed families of east/north lattice paths from $(-j,1)$ to $(\rho_i-i,m)$ with east steps at height $r$ weighted $y_r$, choose the first intersection in a fixed order and exchange the two tails, an involution that preserves the monomial weight and reverses the permutation sign, so all intersecting families cancel; a nonintersecting family forces the identity matching, and the surviving families are exactly the semistandard tableaux, sign $+1$. Hence the coefficient of $x^\nu$ in $\operatorname{ch}_\lambda$ is the Kostka number $K_{\lambda\nu}$; empty and short-row cases are included. [F3, F4, F5, algebra]

Beta determinants and rim-hook signs. Choose $N\ge n$, put $\beta_{a,i}=\lambda^{(a)}_i+N-i$ with zero parts appended, and for a nonnegative integer array $v$ define $\chi(v;x)=\prod_a\det\bigl(h_{v_{a,i}-N+j}(Y_a)\bigr)_{i,j}$. If two entries of one component of $v$ agree the determinant has equal rows and is zero; otherwise sorting that component into strictly decreasing order and writing $\rho_i=v'_i-N+i$ gives $\chi(v;x)=\varepsilon(v)\prod_a s_{\rho^{(a)}}(Y_a)$ with $\varepsilon$ the product of the row-sorting signs, so every coefficient is a signed Kostka multiplicity. A beta move lowering a bead from $v+L$ to an unoccupied $v$ is exactly the removal of a rim hook of length $L$: tracing the southeast boundary shows the strip between the two boundary steps has $L$ boxes, its leg is the number of occupied positions strictly between $v$ and $v+L$, its foot content is $v-N+1$, and the associated sorting sign is $(-1)^{\operatorname{leg}}$; the correspondence is a bijection by the reverse move. [F4, step 1.1, algebra]

The hook side as a complete finite alternating polynomial. Define $B_\lambda(x)$ as the finite alternating sum of step 2.1: for crosscomponent terms, over $a<b$, over beads $i,j$ and lengths $h\le\beta_{a,i}$, of $\chi(\beta-h e_{a,i}+h e_{b,j};x)V(U_az^{\beta_{a,i}-h}-U_bz^{\beta_{b,j}})$; and for same-component terms, over $a$, $i<j$ and $1\le h\le\beta_{a,i}-\beta_{a,j}-1$, of $\chi(\beta-he_{a,i}+he_{a,j};x)V(U_az^{\beta_{a,i}-h}-U_az^{\beta_{a,j}})$; terms whose $\chi$ is the zero polynomial are omitted before any valuation is evaluated. Then $B_\lambda(x)=\sum_{\mu:\lambda\triangleright\mu}J_{\lambda\mu}\operatorname{ch}_\mu(x)$: a crosscomponent move removing from the earlier component $a$ and adding to a later component $b>a$ produces a strictly dominated $\mu$ and occurs exactly once by the bead description; occupied targets give repeated rows and zero; sorting contributes $(-1)^{\text{removed leg}+\text{added leg}}$; and the prefactor $z^{-N+1}$ converts the beta difference to the difference of the deformed foot residues. In one component the two moved beads $i<j$ give a strict dominance decrease precisely for $1\le h<\beta_i-\beta_j$, the exchange case $h=\beta_i-\beta_j$ giving $\mu=\lambda$ and the outward case giving the reverse dominance; occupied intermediate positions again give zero rows, and the range exceeding a component's size gives a repeated or negative bead, hence a zero determinant. Thus no hook pair is lost or added, and the surviving summands are exactly the $J_{\lambda\mu}$ terms. [step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra]

Nonvanishing of every retained foot difference. For a removable rim hook of length $L$ from a partition of size $M+L$ with foot $(h,j)$, one has $-(M+L-1)\le j-h\le M$: every box left of the foot in its row survives, so $j-1\le M$, and $h\le M+L$ gives the lower bound. If $\lambda$ and $\mu$ remove equal-length hooks in distinct components $a\ne b$ to the same remainder with remainder sizes $M_a,M_b$, their foot contents satisfy $|\gamma_x-\gamma_y|\le M_a+M_b+L-1\le n-1$, so the exponent $n(a-b)+\gamma_x-\gamma_y$ is a nonzero integer; in the same component equal foot content and equal length reconstruct the same inverse hook addition, hence would force $\lambda=\mu$, which the strict-dominance terms exclude. Therefore every retained Laurent difference $U_az^u-U_bz^v$ is nonzero in $F(t)$: it is a unit times a nonzero Laurent monomial times $(z^{N}-1)$-type factors and, by [F2], its valuation is finite, being $0$ when the constant residues differ, $1$ in characteristic zero when they agree, and $p^{v_p(N)}$ in characteristic $p$ when they agree. [F2, step 2.1, algebra]

The same-component operator. In the same-component beta sum put $D=\beta_i-\beta_j$ and $k=D-h$, so the valuation is $f(k)=V(z^k-1)$ up to unit factors; swapping the two changed determinant rows shows $\chi(\beta-(D-k)e_i+(D-k)e_j;x)=-\chi(\beta-ke_i+ke_j;x)$. Hence the complete coefficient of $f(k)$ is $-\sum_{i<j:\beta_i-\beta_j>k}\chi(\beta-ke_i+ke_j;x)$, which is the strictly dominance-lowering part of $-p_kp_k^\perp$ on the abstract shape basis, where $p_k^\perp$ lowers an occupied bead by $k$ into an unoccupied nonnegative position with sign $(-1)^{\#\text{crossed beads}}$ and $p_k$ raises a bead by $k$ with the same sign rule; the bead-raising formula follows from the alternant identity $\det(y_r^{\beta_i})\sum_ry_r^k=\sum_i\det(y_r^{\beta_i+k\delta_{ij}})$ divided by the Vandermonde, and the removal map is its transpose. After one removal and one addition a non-diagonal lower-dominance result comes only from distinct beads $i<j$ with $0<k<\beta_i-\beta_j$, occupied intermediate positions giving zero repeated rows and the diagonal being removed by the strict projection; this proves the operator identification integrally, in every characteristic. [step 2.1, algebra]

The crosscomponent operator as exterior currents. On the $N$-fold exterior power of a space with basis $e_0,e_1,\dots$, represent a partition by the ordered wedge of its beta beads and let $E(p,q)$ insert $e_p$ after removing $e_q$, with exterior signs; it vanishes if $q$ is absent or $p$ is occupied, and its sign is the bead-sorting sign. Expanding $E=\text{creation}\cdot\text{contraction}$ gives $[E(p,q),E(r,s)]=\delta_{q,r}E(p,s)-\delta_{p,s}E(r,q)$. The crosscomponent matrix acting on column shape vectors is $J^{\mathrm{cross}}=\sum_{a<b}\sum_{h>0}\sum_{q\ge h,w\ge0}V(U_az^{q-h}-U_bz^w)E_a(q,q-h)E_b(w,w+h)$, a finite operator on each size-$n$ sector; the reverse hook pair has forward current $E_a(q-h,q)E_b(w+h,w)$, and transposing gives exactly this operator with the same signs and valuation. [step 3.1, step 3.2, step 3.3, algebra]

Horizontal strips and their conjugation. With $S e_q=e_{q+1}$ and $H(x)=(I-xS)^{-1}=\sum_{r\ge0}x^rS^r$, whose entry $H_{p,q}$ is $x^{p-q}$ for $p\ge q$ and $0$ otherwise, the matrix of $\wedge^NH(x)$ between $\beta_\mu$ and $\beta_\rho$ is $x^{|\mu|-|\rho|}\det(1_{\beta_{\mu,i}\ge\beta_{\rho,j}})$. Subtracting consecutive columns of the $0/1$ matrix makes its determinant $1$ exactly when $\beta_{\mu,i}\ge\beta_{\rho,i}>\beta_{\mu,i+1}$ for all $i$, i.e. $\mu_i\ge\rho_i\ge\mu_{i+1}$, the horizontal-strip criterion, and $0$ otherwise; so $\Gamma(x)=\wedge^NH(x)$ adds every horizontal strip once with weight $x^{\text{strip size}}$. For a type component $a$, $\Gamma_a(x)=\prod_{b\le a}\Gamma_b(x)$ adds a horizontal strip in every permitted physical component $b\le a$ and leaves the rest unchanged, so the successive $\Gamma_a$ from the empty shape enumerate exactly the flagged semistandard tableaux and give the branching matrix. Conjugation is explicit: since $H^{-1}=I-xS$ has column vector $e_p-xe_{p+1}$ and row covector $\sum_{r\le q}x^{q-r}e_r^*$, $\Gamma(x)^{-1}E(p,q)\Gamma(x)=\sum_{r=0}^qx^{q-r}\bigl(E(p,r)-xE(p+1,r)\bigr),$ and the two-current conjugation is the ordered product of two such sums. [step 4.1, algebra]

The marked-strip factor and the local commutator identity. For a permitted $\Gamma_a$ transition $\rho\to\lambda$ with new-node set $\eta$, put $r_x=U_{\operatorname{comp}(x)}z^{\operatorname{content}(x)}$ and $F^{(a)}_{\lambda\rho}=\prod_{x\in\eta}\prod_{\operatorname{comp}(x)<b\le a}(r_x-U_b)\prod_{\substack{x\in[\rho],\,y\in\eta\\x,y\ \text{same physical row}}}C_+(r_x,r_y)\prod_{\substack{x<y,\ x,y\in\eta\\\text{different physical rows}}}C_+(r_x,r_y)\prod_{\substack{x\in\eta,\,y\in[\rho]\\x<y}}R(r_x,r_y).$ Splitting the node pairs of [F1] into old/old, old/new and new/new pairs shows that along any semistandard chain the product of these factors is exactly $\gamma_{t_T}/(C_{t_T}u_T)$; older labels are smaller than the new label, same-row old/new pairs and same-label new/new pairs give $C_+$, a row-reading-earlier new node before an old node is a different-label inversion giving $R$, and all other pairs give nothing. Then $(J_n\Gamma_a^{(n,m)}-\Gamma_a^{(n,m)}J_m)_{\lambda\rho}=x^{n-m}V(F^{(a)}_{\lambda\rho})$ on permitted transitions and $0$ otherwise, on the reachable prefix sector. On support this is the exact row/column minor computation: the strip matrix is upper unitriangular, the row- and column-replacement determinants are $d_i^{\mathrm{row}}(v)=1_{p_i\le v<p_{i-1}}$ and $d_i^{\mathrm{col}}(v)=1_{q_{i+1}<v\le q_i}$ with $p_0=\infty$, the $J\Gamma$ term of index $j+1$ pairs with the $\Gamma J$ term of index $j$ sharing the bound $K_j=p_{b,j}-q_{b,j+1}-1$, and the elementary interval identity $\sum_{s=0}^{M-1}(\psi(A+s+K+1)-\psi(A+s+1))=\sum_{h=1}^{\min(M,K)}(\psi(A+M+K+1-h)-\psi(A+h))$ matches the two sides term by term, with $\psi(d)=V(U_az^d-U_b)$; the same-component telescoping is the analogue of this computation with the boundary factor. Off support, the defective strip step matrix has rank at most $N-2$, whence both sides vanish, or rank $N-1$ with one missing tail type $[P,P')$ and one duplicated type $(Q',Q]$; then the adjugate is $\varepsilon vu^{\mathsf T}$ with $u=e_i-e_{i+1}$, $v=e_r-e_{r-1}$ and one common sign, and replacing a row or column at position $x$ gives $D_{\mathrm{row}}(x)=\varepsilon u_l1_{P\le x<P'}$ and $D_{\mathrm{col}}(x)=\varepsilon v_l1_{Q'<x\le Q}$, so the a-only, b-only and both-defective cases cancel by the displayed interval translations; in the deficiency-two pattern with duplicate thresholds $r<s$ and missing intervals $I_1,I_2$ strictly between them, the row-side coefficient of $\phi(k)$ is $\varepsilon(A_{I_1}(k)B_{I_2}(k)-A_{I_2}(k)B_{I_1}(k))$ and the column-side coefficient is the same expression after the endpoint-reciprocity substitution $A_{I}=D^-$, $B_{I}=D^+$, so every formal coefficient cancels exactly, including adjacent missing thresholds and overlapping column groups, and higher deficiency kills both sides. [F1, F6, step 3.3, step 4.1, step 5.1, algebra]

Telescoping and the valuation formula. Multiply the $\Gamma$ matrices in increasing type-row-label order and telescope $J\Gamma-\Gamma J$ from $J_0=0$; by step 6.1 each commutator inserts exactly $V(F)$ at its strip position, so the $\lambda$-coordinate of the resulting identity is $\sum_{T}\gamma_{t_T}/(C_{t_T}u_T)=L_\lambda(x)$ on one side and $B_\lambda(x)$ on the other. All padded artificial symbols cancel before the surviving coefficients are evaluated, and every surviving coefficient corresponds to a valid current, hence by step 3.2 to a nonzero foot difference with finite valuation. Comparing with the exact monic product [F1] and the hook side of step 3.1, and taking the coefficient of $x^
u$ at an actual multipartition weight $
u$ (auxiliary compositions only index the same polynomials and never enter the Schur conclusion), gives $V(\det G_{\lambda
u})=\sum_\mu J_{\lambda\mu}K_{\mu
u};$ the empty case $n=0$ gives $0$, all ranks keep the fixed parameters $z=q_Ht$, $U_a=Q_at^{na}$, and arbitrary-composition coefficients are combinatorial only. [F1, step 3.1, step 3.2, step 6.1, algebra] ∎

citations.quote: For $C_n=\operatorname{End}_{H_n}\bigl(\bigoplus_{\lambda}m_\lambda H_n\bigr)$ of [[def-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-cell-and-schur-modules]] over a field $F$ with unit parameters, its standards $\Delta_\lambda$ have nonzero absolutely simple heads $L_\lambda$ indexed by all multipartitions, with $[\Delta_\lambda:L_\lambda]=1$ and $[\Delta_\lambda:L_\mu]\ne0$ only if $\lambda\unrhd\mu$;

Over the fraction field of the universal Laurent parameter ring, all cyclotomic Specht modules are simple and $H_n$ is split semisimple; all Schur standards $\Delta_\lambda$ equal $L_\lambda$ and have nondegenerate cellular forms. Moreover, fix $N\ge1$, a field $F$ with nonzero $q_H,Q_1,\dots,Q_\ell$, and $0\le d\le N$, and take $\mathcal O=F[t,t^{-1}]_{(t-1)}$ with $z=q_Ht$, $U_a=Q_at^{Na}$.
Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $n\ge0$ and $\ell\ge1$, and let $z,U_1,\dots,U_\ell$ be units of $R$ ([[def-algebra-over-a-commutative-ring]]).

Work with the arbitrary-level Murphy/Schur datum of [[def-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-cell-and-schur-modules]] over either (i) the fraction field $K$ of the universal Laurent parameter ring, including the generic field of the Lyle–Mathas deformation, or (ii) any field $F$ with nonzero $q_H,Q_1,\dots,Q_\ell$ under the deformation $z=q_Ht$, $U_a=Q_at^{na}$ in $F(t)$.

Fix any field $F$, level $\ell\ge1$, $q_H\in F^\times$ of finite order $e\ge2$, charges $Q_a=q_H^{c_a}$, $n\ge0$, and the Lyle–Mathas parameters $\mathcal O=F[t,t^{-1}]_{(t-1)}$, $z=q_Ht$, $U_a=Q_at^{na}$, with $V=\nu_{t-1}\circ(-)$.

Let $O$ be a discrete valuation ring with uniformizer $\pi$ and residue field $F=O/\pi O$ ([[def-discrete-valuation-ring]]), and let $\nu_\pi$ denote its valuation. Let $M$ be a finite free $O$-module with an $O$-valued bilinear pairing $b$ ([[def-left-and-right-modules]]) whose scalar extension to $\operatorname{Frac}(O)$ is nondegenerate.

Let $O$ be a discrete valuation ring with uniformizer $\pi$ and residue field $F$, and let $M$ be a finite free $O$-module with an $O$-valued bilinear form $b$ whose scalar extension to $\operatorname{Frac}(O)$ is nondegenerate, as in [[lem-dvr-cellular-jantzen-filtration-and-gram-valuation]] (the "(DVR leaf)").

Let $\mathcal C$ be an essentially small abelian category ([[def-abelian-category]]). Its set of isomorphism classes is denoted $\operatorname{Iso}(\mathcal C)$. The **Grothendieck group** of $\mathcal C$ is $$ G_0(\mathcal C):=\mathbb Z[\operatorname{Iso}(\mathcal C)]\big/\langle e_Y-e_X-e_Z:\ 0\to X\to Y\to Z\to 0\text{ is short exact in }\mathcal C\rangle.

Let $F$ be a field, let $F[t,t^{-1}]$ be its Laurent polynomial ring ([[def-the-laurent-polynomial-ring]]), and let $v_1$ be the $(t-1)$-adic valuation on the nonzero elements of $F[t,t^{-1}]$: for $0\ne f$, $$v_1(f):=\max\{n\ge0:(t-1)^n\mid f\ \text{in}\ F[t,t^{-1}]\},$$ so that $v_1(f)=0$ exactly when $f(1)\ne0$ ([[def-discrete-valuation-ring]]).

derivations.claim: Filtration and radical. For $n=0$ there is one empty multipartition, $S_{\mathcal O}=\mathcal O$, $\Delta_{\mathcal O}=\mathcal O$ with form $1$, every positive filtration term is $0$, and every $J$ coefficient is $0$, so the assertions follow directly. For $n\ge1$, [F1] gives free standard lattices with nondegenerate generic forms. The Smith reduction of [F4] shows that the defined filtration is by $S_F$-submodules, begins at $\Delta_F(\lambda)$, has first term equal to the form radical, and is zero for all sufficiently large $s$. The rank-one cell actions of the nonzero cellular form force every proper submodule into that radical, so the first term is the module radical. [given, F1, F4]

The auxiliary character identity. Introduce ordered variables for the type-row labels; the auxiliary generating series of flagged semistandard tableaux is the product over physical components $a$ of $s_{\lambda^{(a)}}(Y_a)$, where $Y_a$ is the alphabet of type components at least $a$, and its coefficient at an actual multipartition $\nu$ is $K_{\lambda\nu}$. Successive $\Gamma_a$ matrices add the horizontal strips carrying each next label and therefore enumerate these tableaux once; the path/Jacobi–Trudi cancellation proves this character identity locally. No actual Schur weight or module for another composition is needed. [F1, F3]

The weight-character reduction. Fix an actual multipartition weight $
u$. The selfadjoint orthogonal decomposition by $e_
u$ makes the standard weight space orthogonal to every other weight space, so [F4] gives $\sum_{s>0}\dim_Fe_
u\Delta_F(\lambda)^s=V(\det G_{\lambda
u})$. By [F2] and additivity of the valuation this is the sum over type-$
u$ semistandard $T$ of the valuations of their explicit monic norms; empty weight spaces use determinant $1$ and contribute $0$. [F2, F4, step 1.1]

The beta form of the hook side. Pad the beta lists to $N>n$. Removing a hook of length $h$ lowers one beta bead by $h$ with sorting sign $(-1)^{\operatorname{leg}}$, and adding it raises a bead by $h$ with the corresponding sign; the foot content is the lowered bead position minus $N$ plus $1$, up to the unit foot-residue shift. Thus the full signed equal-length hook side is precisely the finite shifted-beta Jacobi–Trudi polynomial: same-component inward ranges, crosscomponent earlier-to-later ranges, occupied-position zero terms and the unit shift are all covered by [F3]. Its coefficient at $\nu$ is $\sum_\mu J_{\lambda\mu}K_{\mu\nu}$. [F3, step 1.2]

Telescoping the marked-strip commutator. The rank $m=0$ case has a single empty partition and needs no block theorem. [F1, F3, F4, F5]

If the component weights differ, choose a component whose weight exceeds its target and one whose weight is deficient; a positive-weight component has a removable $e$-hook by its core construction [F5]. For any prescribed foot residue $f$, moving the lowest bead on runner $f-1$ down by $e$ creates an $e$-hook with that foot residue, since its foot residue is the starting beta position plus one; wrap this hook in the deficient component with the same foot residue. The changed components determine the removed and added hook pair uniquely, and in the appropriate dominance orientation their $J$ contribution is one signed valuation with no cancellation; equal foot residues mean the nonzero generic difference is divisible by $t-1$, so the valuation is a positive integer. Thus the transfer is a Jantzen edge; it lowers the sum of squares of the discrepancies of the component hook weights by at least $2$, so finitely many such transfers equalize the component weights. Composing the two finite chains connects any two multipartitions of rank $n$ with equal componentwise $e$-cores, proving that they are $J$-equivalent; the fixed-size comparison of coefficients is step 2.1. Declare each image of a homogeneous KLR generator to be homogeneous of the same degree; the images generate $H^\Lambda_\alpha$ and the KLR relations of [F2] are homogeneous, so the resulting degree assignment is well defined. Products retain degree addition because $\rho$ is an algebra map, so the degree summands are exactly the transported homogeneous summands. Since the generator images span the algebra, their assigned degrees determine every degree summand and give uniqueness of the grading for that fixed choice, with $\deg e(i)=0$, $\deg y_r=2$ and $\deg\psi_re(i)=-a_{i_r,i_{r+1}}$. If $\rho'$ is the isomorphism attached to another admissible series, then $\rho'\circ\rho^{-1}$ sends each homogeneous native generator image of the first choice to the corresponding new image and hence is graded by construction; the two transported algebras are graded-isomorphic, while the underlying identity map on $H^\Lambda_\alpha$ need not be graded because the two series differ by units that need not be homogeneous of degree zero. Triviality is not excluded. Assigning degree zero to every ordinary Hecke generator makes all defining relations homogeneous, so the degree-zero assignment is a legitimate transported grading and no impossibility statement is asserted. Conversely $e(0,1)=1$, $y_2=t$, $y_1=\psi_1=0$ in $F[t]/(t^2)$ satisfy all rank-two relations, so that sector is $F[t]/(t^2)$ with $\deg t=2$, and its Brundan–Kleshchev image supplies an actual nontrivial transported grading, including in the characteristic-two degeneration. This is a witness that the construction can be nontrivial, not a claim about all sectors. [F1, F2, step 1.1]

Distinct powers of the generator are linearly independent, so each is infinite dimensional, whereas every cyclotomic block $H^\Lambda_\alpha$ is finite dimensional of dimension at most $\ell^dd!$ by the bounded spanning family [F2]. Hence no cyclotomic KLR block is isomorphic to the whole affine Hecke algebra. [F1, F2, algebra]
